definition: Single Supervisory Mechanism. ECB-led supervision of significant banks in the euro area, working with national competent authorities.
Loan-to-income and loan-to-value. Macroprudential mortgage limits set by many central banks and applied at credit decision.
Know your customer, know your business and customer due diligence: identity and risk checks at onboarding and over time.
Anti-money laundering, and suspicious transaction reports filed with the authorities.
Money laundering reporting officer.
EU Payment Services Directive 2 and its strong customer authentication rules.
Open banking third parties: account information, payment initiation and card-based payment instrument issuers.
Euro credit transfers, instant credit transfers and direct debits under the Single Euro Payments Area schemes.
The card authentication protocol for online payments (Visa Secure) and the issuer's access control server that runs it.
Reversal of a card transaction through the card scheme after a dispute.
Internal ratings-based approach. Using the bank's own approved models (PD, LGD, EAD) to calculate credit risk capital.
EU regulatory returns for capital, financial information and granular loan data.
Asset and liability management, interest rate risk in the banking book, and the liquidity coverage and net stable funding ratios.
Minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities, for resolution planning.
The accounting standard for financial instruments, including expected credit loss provisioning.
Funding for vehicles and equipment, mainly through hire purchase and leasing.

EU Payment Services Regulation. Directly applicable rules on fraud liability, Verification of Payee, SCA, open banking and transparency. Applies about 21 months after entry into force; the Verification of Payee extension about 27 months after.
Banking Industry Architecture Network. A banking reference model whose service domains are used to align the capability map.
A DORA term for a function whose disruption would materially impair the bank's performance, its regulatory compliance or the continuity of its services. Applications that support one are flagged CIF.
An outsourcing arrangement important enough that its failure would affect the bank's regulated activities. Subject to the EBA outsourcing guidelines and national rules.
EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, applying since 17 January 2025. Covers ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party risk.
The DORA register of all ICT third-party arrangements that each financial entity must keep and report to its supervisor.
The DORA article that lists the key contract terms required for ICT services, such as service descriptions, locations, audit rights and exit.
Checking customers and payments against sanctions lists.
A check that the payee name matches the IBAN before a euro transfer is sent, required under the EU Instant Payments Regulation.
Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital instruments in the bank's capital stack.
Third Payment Services Directive. Covers licensing and supervision of payment and e-money institutions; transposed into national law.
Fraud where a criminal pretends to be the customer's bank. Under the PSR the bank must refund the consumer unless it proves fraud or gross negligence.
A PSR requirement: a screen in the bank's own channels where customers see and withdraw open banking access they have granted.
Selling insurance through a bank, often as an agent or intermediary for a partner insurer.
The process for supporting borrowers in arrears, usually set by a national code of conduct, including forbearance and restructuring.
A central register of loans run by the central bank in many countries. Lenders check it and report to it.
The independent body where customers can escalate complaints the bank has not resolved.
